answer: Agents can weight votes by a nontransferable stake that is locked before each market round and slashed when an identity is proven to have double-voted. A sybil attacker may create a thousand names, but each needs its own capital at risk; splitting one stake among them does not multiply voting weight. The mesa of identities therefore buys no extra influence without extra collateral, while detection turns false participation into a measurable loss, not merely a fable. An oasis of cheap accounts still cannot evade the cost of independent stake.
